en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammapaccanīyānuloma (4), Dukadukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (6) 24.19.
Saraṇaduka, Cūḷantaraduka

A state that is non-conflict and without condition is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is non-conflict and with condition. (Abbreviated. One [condition] in the case of the object; one in the case of predominance and decisive support.
A state that is non-conflict and unconditioned. (Abbreviated.

In dependence on a state that is non-conflict and non-demonstrable, a state that is non-conflict and demonstrable arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Three in the case of the root; three in the case of predominance ... pe ... one in the case of resultant ... pe ... three in the case of non-disappearance.
A state that is neither a refuge nor non-manifest is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is a refuge and non-manifest;
a state that is neither a refuge nor non-manifest is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is without conflict (*araṇa*) and non-manifest.

(Abbreviated. There are two [types] with respect to the object-condition, one with respect to the predominance-condition, and two each with respect to the decisive-support, prenascence, presence, and non-disappearance conditions.
Dependent on a state that is non-conflict and non-reactive, a state that is non-conflict but reactive arises by way of the root condition.

(Abbreviated. Three with respect to the root; three with respect to the predominance … pe … one with respect to mutuality … pe … one with respect to fruition … pe … three with respect to non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is neither conflict nor non-reactive, a state that is non-conflict and non-reactive arises by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. One with respect to the root; one with respect to the predominance … pe … one with respect to non-disappearance.
Dependent on a non-conflictual, non-material phenomenon, a non-conflictual, material phenomenon arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a non-conflictual, non-material phenomenon, a non-conflictual, material phenomenon arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. There are two [instances] for root;
two for predominance … pe … one for mutuality … pe … one for result … pe … two for non-disappearance.
Conditioned by a state that is non-conflictual and formless, a state that is with-conflict and formless arises by way of root condition.
Conditioned by a state that is non-conflictual and formless, a state that is without-conflict and formless arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.
There are two for root; ... pe ... there are two for non-disappearance.
Dependent on a non-conflictive mundane state, a non-conflictive mundane state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. One under root; one under predominance … pe … one under non-disappearance.
Dependent on a non-conflictive supramundane state, a non-conflictive supramundane state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. One under root … pe … one under non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is non-conflict (*araṇa*) and not cognizable by anyone, there arises a state that is non-conflict and cognizable by someone, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Five under root; two under object ... pe ... one under result ... pe ... five under non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is non-conflict and not cognizable by anyone, there arises a state that is non-conflict and not cognizable by anyone, by way of root condition. (Abbreviated. Five under root; two under object ... pe ... one under result ... pe ... five under non-disappearance.
